title: Grid
cards/0/body:
Grid splits space into rows and columns. There are three ways to set a column's width:

200: exactly 200 pixels.
Auto: as much as the content needs.
*: a share of the remaining space. 2* gets twice as much as *.
cards/0/code:
<Grid ColumnDefinitions="Auto,*,2*" RowDefinitions="Auto,*">
  <TextBlock Grid.Row="0" Grid.Column="0" Text="Icons"/>
  <ListBox   Grid.Row="1" Grid.Column="1"/>
</Grid>
cards/1/task: The menu on the left is always 200 px, and the content takes everything else. Check it at both window widths.
cards/2/q: The window is 800 px, columns are "200,*". How much does the second column get?
cards/2/explain: The star takes whatever is left after fixed and Auto columns: 800 − 200.
cards/3/task: The icon column fits its content exactly (48 px), and the list is twice as wide as the properties panel.
cards/4/q: Columns "*,2*,*" in an 800 px window. What are the widths?
cards/4/explain: There are 4 shares in total, so one share is 200 px.
cards/5/title: The short syntax is an Avalonia perk
cards/5/body:
In WPF, columns take a lot of typing: one ColumnDefinition tag each. In Avalonia you can use a string: ColumnDefinitions="Auto,*,2*".

You place an element in a cell with Grid.Row and Grid.Column (counting from zero), and span several with Grid.ColumnSpan.
cards/6/q: A button in the second column of the first row
cards/6/explain: Counting starts at zero: the second column is Column="1".
cards/7/q: What happens to an Auto column if its content gets wider?
cards/7/options/0: The column grows, and the star columns get narrower
cards/7/explain: Auto adapts to its content; stars share what is left.
cards/8/q: Match each value to its meaning
cards/9/q: What is true? Select all that apply.
cards/9/options/0: ColumnDefinitions can be set with a string
cards/9/options/2: Stars share the space left after fixed and Auto columns
cards/9/explain: Auto fits the content. It is not a fixed number.
